---
title: "Interactive chemistry: one exploration for each study day"
---

Use these short explorations alongside the drawings and paper problems.
Predict what will happen before changing a control; then explain the chemical
reason for the change. Most demos fit a 5–10 minute classroom or independent
activity. They support the existing 45-minute sessions and practice route.

Every demo has a direct link in the left sidebar under its corresponding
unit or mixed-practice day. No account, R session or external service is needed.

## Use a model with its assumptions

The diagrams, curves and supplied observations are teaching models. A slider
does not establish a measured reaction rate, experimental spectrum or isolated
product identity. Each page states the model assumptions and links back to its
local chemistry explanation and paper practice. For example, the extraction
explorer supplies partition assumptions that an aqueous ionisation curve alone
does not contain.

The demos keep their state in your current browser page and do not submit
answers or record students. Use reset/preset controls to compare situations,
and return to the paper question to construct your own drawing or explanation.
